title: Revelation Density S-Curve Test

canonical_node.axiom: Revelation density in biblical text follows a logistic growth curve over time.
definitions: Revelation density: information content per unit of text across biblical eras, measured using compression-based complexity proxies.
Sigmoid curve: a logistic function R(t) = R_max / (1 + exp(-k(t - t0))).
Biblical eras: sequential periods of biblical history as defined in the test.
derivation: The chi-field's K component predicts logistic growth for revelation density.
Logistic growth is expected when growth is limited by carrying capacity.
Measure revelation density per era using compression-based proxies.
Fit the era sequence to a sigmoid curve and evaluate R.
Compare sigmoid fit to linear and exponential fits.
canonical_node.action: Compute revelation density across biblical eras, fit to a sigmoid, and assess fit quality.
boundary: Does not claim to prove divine action.
Does not make claims about canon.
Does not establish the chi-field model's validity.
Does not measure revelation itself, only text information structure.
test: R of sigmoid fit is high and better than linear and exponential fits.
Inflection point falls in mid-prophetic period.

dg1_dependencies: Compression-based complexity measurement method (from Tests 03 and 06).
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a quantitative test of the S-curve prediction for revelation density.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the empirical observation that the biblical text has non-random information structure.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this test, the empirical support for the logistic growth prediction is weakened.

classification.recommended_atom_action: preserve as empirical observation; do not treat as proof of chi-field

overstatement_risks: Interpreting a curve fit as evidence for the chi-field model.
Assuming the measurement proxies accurately reflect revelation density.
Overgeneralizing from a single test to the entire framework.
kill_conditions: If the sigmoid fit is not reproducible.
If alternative models fit equally well or better.
If the measurement method is shown to be biased.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the curve fitting and statistical comparison in Lean.

plain_summary: This document reports a test that fits a sigmoid curve to the density of revelatory content across biblical eras, claiming a good fit. It is an empirical observation, not a proof of the underlying theory.
